, lies Tsugash, a land known for its beauty and bloodshed. It features emerald forests, mist-laden coasts, and old and snowcapped peaks. Despite the natural splendor, the people of Tsugash live in a state of tension. Clans, city-states, and wandering war bands clash over old grudges and diverging beliefs. The continent’s story is one of breathtaking abundance paired with unending struggle.

Though some regions lean temperate, all four seasons arrive in full force across Tsugash. Winters sweep down from the northern ranges, coating the land in snow and turning mountain passes into treacherous corridors. Spring bursts forth with wildflowers and rushing rivers that carve through fertile valleys. Summers are warm and bright, drawing laborers into the open fields. Autumn sees that the forests turn red and gold before the first snows return.
Tsugash is home to many peoples, but

form its cultural backbone. Their societies are as varied as the terrain they inhabit. Ancient Orcish clans trace their bloodlines back centuries, guarding traditions of honor, ancestor worship, and martial discipline.

are a relatively new inhabitant, immigrating to Tsugash after the war, and causing some discontent in the process. Over time, Orcish clans have lost power as sovereign democracies form, but some refuse to lose the power they obtained generations ago.

Humans are the stubborn descendants of the
who turned against their gods during the War and were stripped of their divine birthright. Banished from
to the harsh northern continent of
as punishment, they have quietly grown in isolation while maintaining tight-knit communities that have never forgotten their fallen past.
Though most remain in their northern homeland, adventurous or outcast Humans can be found across Raasha working as sailors, mercenaries, and laborers. Tempered by generations in
’s unforgiving wilderness, Humans are notoriously persistent, driven, and quick to hold a grudge—yet deeply reliant on the strength of their own communities.
Humans bear a striking resemblance to their

ancestors, though they lack their cosmic longevity and star-touched features. Their skin, hair, and eye tones are more grounded and muted, and they tend to possess slightly broader, stockier builds than average
, while remaining comparable in stature to the other mortal peoples of Raasha.
Ardona is a small continent in the Northern Hemisphere, curving westward as it stretches north. Its southern edge meets the oceanic waters of Athera’s Strait, a natural divide from the continent of
. The terrain shifts from coastal cliffs and windswept lowlands to craggy highlands and deep glens, growing harsher the farther north one travels.
Though remote, Ardona is not stagnant. Trade routes hug the coast, and strategic passes in the narrowing north are fiercely contested.

Ardona’s climate is a study in severity and contrast, defined by its tapering geography and relentless northern winds. The southern reaches, closest to Athera’s Strait, experience cool maritime conditions—frequent rain, biting gusts, and short summers that allow for hardy crops from rocky soil. Fog rolls in from the strait, cloaking the coastlines, while inland valleys remain damp year-round.

As one travels northward, the land rises and the climate grows increasingly harsh and unforgiving. Winters are long and brutal, with snowdrifts swallowing roads and frost overstaying its welcome. The highlands are home to violent storms, sudden temperature drops, and a near-constant wind that howls through passes and ravines. Even in summer, warmth is fleeting.

This climate has shaped a culture of resilience and austerity. Architecture favors thick stone walls and turf roofs; clothing is layered, woolen, and built for durability. The people of Ardona know the weather not as a condition, but as a constant presence and force to be respected. It is said that the wind remembers the betrayal that brought them here, and that the cold is the land’s way of keeping them humble.
of Ardona are the descendants of

, cast down and stripped of their celestial birthright. Banished to the cold reaches of the north, they first settled in the southern lowlands. Over generations, they pushed northward, driven by ambition and resentment, taming the native fauna, and conquering scattered
clans who once roamed the highlands. These Primordial-born peoples were subdued and forcibly assimilated—now their customs survive only in fragments, buried beneath the dominant

But unity did not last. A brutal civil war split the exiled into two nations: the south, proud of its ancestral settlements and wary of change, and the north, forged in conquest and hardened by frontier life. Though they share blood, the two nations now stand divided by ideology, memory, and the lingering question of who truly carries the legacy of the fallen divine. The
, though silenced, reside beneath the surface—neither fully erased nor entirely accepted.

Saurian society is shaped by cooperation, practical skill, and a deep respect for the natural world. Their settlements are modest but well‑adapted to their environments, built from local materials and arranged around communal spaces where food, labor, and responsibility are shared. While each subrace (and each community) has its own customs and ways of life, all Saurians value self‑sufficiency and the bonds they share with their kin. Their communities may appear primitive to outsiders, but they are resilient, resourceful, and deeply rooted in the lands they inhabit.

Saurians vary widely in appearance, but all share scaled skin, animalistic athleticism and senses, and features shaped by their environments. Together, they form a diverse but unified people whose forms reflect the places they call home.

Rivers carve through the forest's undergrowth like veins of silver, feeding sprawling wetlands. Beyond the rainforests, adventurous explorers can hike across volcanic cliffs or through grasslands nestled in mountain valleys.

Sa Zortao’s climate is a symphony of heat and moisture, shaped by its position in the southern tropics. The continent’s jungles flourish with humidity, where rain falls in thick sheets. Monsoon cycles bring floods, saturate the canopy, and summon blooms so vivid they seem otherworldly.

Highlands and volcanic plateaus offer cooler air, while savannas and dry forests stretch across the rain-shadowed interior, marked by seasonal fires and golden grasses. Coastal regions are warm and stormy, shaped by ocean currents and salt-laden winds. Across Sa Zortao, the climate is studied, woven into ritual calendars and agricultural cycles.

Festivals mark solstices and eclipses, when drums echo through the jungle and sacred fires burn for days.

Elves are magical beings born of materialized spirits. When creatures on Raasha die, traces of their memories and experiences linger in the spiritual world. Ages ago, a powerful sorceress learned to harness this essence and reform it into new life. It remains a sacred ritual still practiced today. When an Elf is born naturally instead, they inherit fragments of memories directly from their family line.

Connected to the spirit world, Elves possess an innate magic that lets them sense and shape its currents. Their collective memories give them a deep appreciation for knowledge and a reverence for tradition. Like Dwarves, most Elves rarely stray far from their homelands. They often speak in a thoughtful, measured tone, and their spiritual awareness lends them a serene, calming presence.

Elves are slightly smaller than average humanoids due to their slender frames. While they resemble Humans in many ways, they have pointed ears, sharp features, and an ageless appearance. Remarkably agile and light on their feet, their movements carry an effortless grace.

- When they dream, Dreamwalker Elves sometimes live through the memories of spirits. They perceive these dreams in real time, with a single rest feeling like days or weeks spent living another's long-lost life. This constant influx of historical perspectives leaves them deeply introspective, possessing an uncanny wisdom. Sometimes called Night Elves or
, they have skin in grayish hues of blue or purple.

- By studying the flow of the spirit world, Fateweaver Elves read the collective mass of Raasha's memories to divine what is to come. Viewing history as a repeating tapestry, they sense the spiritual momentum of past choices to anticipate danger before it strikes. Commonly called High Elves, they are typically taller than other Elves and possess a calculating foresight.

Attuned to forgotten voices, Spiritspeaker Elves act as direct bridges between the living world and wandering spirits. Through painted runes or carved totems, they can allow the dead to speak through them or perform rituals to commune with nature spirits. Commonly known as Wood Elves due to their northern forest kingdoms, they possess warm, earthy hair and skin tones.

Genasi are the first descendants of the Primordial titans, the godlike beings who shaped the world long before written history. As one of the three Elder Races, they once stood alongside the
in unity. Their three subraces, Flora, Fauna, and Terrana, each carry the spark of a different titan, giving them a natural tie to the lands and living forces their ancestors watched over.

Since the war, the Genasi have suffered more than most. Their cities fell, their numbers dwindled, and many were forced into a nomadic life. Today, most Genasi travel in small tribes, moving with the seasons and relying on tight‑knit communities for survival. Only a few settlements remain fully under their control, and even those are scattered across distant regions. Though they once held vast territories, Genasi are now found all over the world, often far from the lands their subraces once called home.

Goliaths were the second race shaped by the old Primordial gods, created after the
but with a very different purpose. Where the

embodied the raw forces of the natural world, Goliaths were forged to endure those forces. Though they can wield elemental power, their true gift lies in surviving it, channeling it, and refusing to break beneath it. This distinction has long fueled a rivalry with the
, a race they once warred against, whose own elemental abilities and imposing stature often invite comparison neither race appreciates.

Goliath culture is built on challenge, blunt honesty, and the pursuit of personal glory and exceptionalism. It is common—expected, even—for young Goliaths to leave their clans and seek a name for themselves. Long ago, their people were subjugated by the Giants, forced into labor and hardship until they eventually won their freedom. Because of this history, Goliaths still speak the Giant tongue, though many use it reluctantly. They are famously competitive, measuring themselves and others through feats of strength, endurance, or courage, and while they respect their ancient connection to the Primordials, they strongly dislike being compared to their Genasi kin.

Goliaths are the largest of all humanoid races, towering over others with broad frames and powerful builds. Their skin ranges through shades of gray and brown, and their inky black eyes often carry speckles or thin veins of color that stand out against their features. Natural markings run across their skin in patterns reminiscent of tattoos, typically indicating the clan or family they come from.
- Volcanic Goliaths are acclimated to eruption zones, enduring blistering heat, acidic steam, and toxic volcanic gases that would kill most others.
- Typhonic Goliaths are shaped by storm fronts that feature freezing blizzards, sky‑splitting lightning, and thunderous shockwaves.

The War for Raasha was a planet-spanning conflict that shattered the ancient age of divine harmony. Triggered by a covert betrayal among the gods, the decades-long war devastated mortal civilizations, scarred the realm's natural landscapes, and permanently severed the deities from walking directly alongside their creations.
Following the pact between the pantheons, three elder races were brought into existence: the
. For an era, these lineages flourished under the direct guidance of their creators, establishing grand civilizations before giving rise to subsequent mortal races.
Unbeknownst to the realm, however, an enigmatic faction of celestial pursuers—the former clan of the
—had tracked the renegades to Raasha. Watching from the shadows, these pursuers secretly infiltrated both mortal societies and the native pantheons, subtly sowing discord, jealousy, and suspicion.
The secret orchestration culminated in a catastrophic betrayal, turning factions within the native pantheons against the

and plunging the entire planet into war. Spanning decades, the conflict saw the rise and fall of countless mortal alliances, the destruction of ancient cities, and the divine empowerment or arcane ascension of extraordinary individuals who claimed godhood amidst the chaos.

As the catastrophic power of the gods irreversibly scarred the land and fractured the bonds between races, a desperate coalition of mortals took drastic action. Prioritizing the planet's survival over divine loyalty, this group enacted a grand ritual that sealed all pantheons away from Raasha behind an impenetrable cosmic veil.

In the post-war era, the physical presence of the gods on Raasha came to an end. Skill Challenges measure a group’s ability to work together to execute a complex plan, survive a hazardous environment, or overcome a multi-stage obstacle.

To complete a Skill Challenge, the party must accumulate a target number of successes before reaching a specific threshold of failures (for example, 5 successes before 3 failures to escape a collapsing two-story dungeon, or 7 successes before 3 failures for a larger three-story dungeon). Players act in turns, with each turn allowing a player to make a check or expend a resource toward the party's goal.

Players are encouraged to rely on their heroic archetypes by utilizing skills in which they have proficiency. A player may attempt a check using a skill in which they lack proficiency, but doing so significantly increases the Difficulty Class (DC) of the check.

An individual character cannot use the same skill more than once during a single Skill Challenge. However, different characters may use the same skill (for example, two different players may both attempt an Athletics check during separate turns).

A player may sacrifice a spell slot or a limited-use feature (such as Channel Divinity or a Superiority Die) to contribute to the challenge. Depending on the resource used and its relevance to the situation, the DM determines whether the effort grants Advantage on the check or bypasses the check entirely to award an automatic success.

Reaching the failure threshold does not always result in a Total Party Wipe or complete failure. Instead, it often introduces significant setbacks, lingering complications, lost time/resources, or immediate new hazards that the party must now face.

The Emerald Reach, also known as "The Reach", is a collection of scattered archipelagos and atolls that stretch between the shores of southeastern

. The Reach is a maritime melting pot, where trading colonies, sovereign city-states, tribal enclaves, and criminal outposts can all be found. Hopping from one island to another shows the diversity of the region. Bays of coral, limestone spires, and mangrove trees punctuate the sea, while reefs and shoals make many channels treacherous, making skilled pilots worth their weight in gold.

Islands within The Reach are home to ancient ruins and dilapidated holy sites, offering lost magic and untold wealth to those who dare excavate them. Local markets carry exotic goods, taverns overflow with multilingual rumors, and pirates, privateers, and opportunists create and break alliances depending on the tide. It's a place where law is negotiable, fortunes can be made in a night, and nearly anything can be bought, stolen, or bargained for.

The Emerald Reach has a warm, tropical climate tempered by sea breezes and seasonal storms, with near-constant humidity, sun-drenched days, and relentless downpours. Trade winds sweep across open channels, cooling coasts and driving predictable currents that sailors exploit for fast passage and pirates for sudden raids. A wet season brings long monsoon rains and swollen rivers that reshape shorelines and reveal or swallow coastal secrets. Cyclonic storms sweep in from the open ocean with little warning and leave shorelines scoured and reefs rearranged.
The Emerald Reach is culturally plural and socially unstable, inhabited by descendants and outcasts from

, island natives, nomadic traders, pirate crews, reef-faring tribes, and mixed communities born of necessity and convenience. City-states prize cunning captains, chartered companies, and merchant councils who broker access to trade routes and legal cover. Tribal peoples maintain ancestral rites tied to tides and storms, while native communities preserve displaced languages, craft traditions, and clandestine networks of kinship. Criminal enclaves run smuggling hubs and black markets that move contraband, relics, and forbidden knowledge. Social status is fluid and often tied to sea-skills, secrecy, and access to networks. Outsiders can rise quickly by proving usefulness, and established powers fall just as fast when a favored captain betrays a patron or a storm drowns a haven. The Reach’s diversity breeds creativity and danger in equal measure.

Aasimar are angelic mortals infused with a divine connection to the stars and moons beyond Raasha, recognized by many as one of the three Elder Races. Though most cannot consciously wield their celestial gifts, all Aasimar experience prescient dreams that echo their cosmic heritage. Aasimar often look to the night's sky for guidance, divining with constellations and trying to connect with their creators.

Aasimar commonly bear features reminiscent of the cosmos: radiant eyes, metallic skin, or moonlit veins. In stature, they are generally comparable to other mortal peoples of Raasha. Each year an Aasimar lives, a faint star-shaped mark appears somewhere on their body. As these soft, dull lights accumulate with age, they form a personal tattoo-like constellation. Many spend their lives seeking a meaning hidden within their sign.

Being one of the three Elder Races, Dragonborn appear as bipedal versions of their draconic ancestors, carrying both the physical presence and elemental power of the ancient dragons. Their ability to exhale elemental energy makes them natural arcanists, but they are just as well known for their legendary warriors as for their sorcerers.

, their jungle homeland, though some clans have migrated to distant lands for reasons unknown to outsiders. Their historic cities rise from canopies and mountainsides with towering temples and bold monuments, each one a testament to their pride and long memory. Dragonborn are passionate people, famous for their vibrant festivals and equally famous for their quick tempers.

Dragonborn are tall, muscular, and covered in scales, with horned heads and vibrant feathers. Their facial structure and general appearance is that of a dragon in humanoid form. The color of their scales reveals the element they were born to wield and exhale. Their lifespan is average among the peoples of Raasha and shorter than their Elder Race kin, but they live with a fierce intensity, as if every day might be their last.

For the last few months, Dulyn Sopuzzo of Sopuzzo Mercantile has been preparing for a voyage to the Emerald Reach. He's hired Captain Romega and a crew to help him find the fabled Sunken Tower — local folktales tell of a powerful Dragonborn sorcerer who built the tower so he could commune with the gods, and many say it's full of powerful, enchanted relics.

While Captain Romega was hiring a crew for The Wishbone, he put out specific postings for people who could protect the ship, her crew, and lead landing parties or scout ahead. Each member of The Party was individually hired as a member of that four-man crew.

The first goal of the voyage, in the eyes of Dulyn Sopuzzo, is to find the pieces of a celestial astrolabe, a tool that arcanists believe was used by the Dragonborn sorcerer. Dulyn believes it is the key to finding the tower.

After a few weeks at sea, The Wishbone's crew finally found one specific island Dulyn was looking for. He paid for a treasure map that detailed a hidden cache used by an old pirate lord and one piece of the astrolabe is believed to be there.

The Party was asked to accompany Dulyn to the island, and raid the cache. Once on shore, they found no signs of recent activity. After a brief time searching for the cache, said to be hidden between three fruit trees, U'll was able to locate it by climbing a large palm tree and surveying the small island. Rushing to the location, Dulyn started digging and promptly found a locked hatch. Haku broke the hatch, which opened to a short underground passage leading to the cache.

Once inside, the party found rotten food stores, old rum, and three medium-sized chests. Inside two were a pirate's haul: gems, jewelry, and other fine treasures. Inside the third was the astrolabe piece Dulyn was looking for — a brass ring, two feet in diameter, with carvings of the lunar cycle inside. The ring was wrapped in cloth and kept with a small scroll written in old Draconic. Dulyn mentioned to the party that Kaavik would be able to decipher its meaning with enough time.

As the party lifted the chests to leave, a trap was sprung! The support beams began to crumble, and toxic gas was filling the area. To survive the trap, the party needed to survive a skill challenge (DC: 4 successes, 3 failures). After 3 successes and 2 failures, everything fell on U'll's last roll. He cunningly produced a large gust of wind to briefly clear out the toxic gas, giving the party just enough time to escape with minimal treasure and the astrolabe piece.

While some precious treasure was lifted from the cache, Nix secretly gave himself the largest cut, leaving a bigger cut for The Party, and an even smaller cut for the rest of the crew. Nobody noticed, but Canto did see him alone, partitioning the treasure, causing him to metaphorically raise an eyebrow.
After the successful raid, Dulyn told the crew to anchor near the bay, and campout on the beach. They broke out some extra rations and had a night of games, story, and drinking.

Noticing some of the sailors dueling each other with makeshift swords, Nix asked if he could duel the winner. Between trying to go easy on the man who had clearly not professionally handled a sword, and the distractions that U'll was making, the fight ended up being closer than Nix would have liked. In the last moment, Nix found an opportunity to score his last point, but a loss of temper caused him to strike the sailor with excessive force. Although he won the duel against an untrained opponent, he managed to make himself look like an unhinged member of the crew. Canto, Nix, and Haku all saw the damage he caused. Later in the evening, Canto brought up the fight, mentioning that truly mastering one's power is knowing when to use it, leaving Nix to contemplate his actions. Haku performed a small Lay On Hands to cure the sailor's broken ribs, leaving him feeling better, but gobsmacked at the miracle.
Gordot was telling stories to the crew, and Haku was able to better his relationship with Bensi, bonding over their shared Elven heritage.

In the middle of the night, U'll woke up to a heavy cloud of fog rolling in on the beach. Seeing that one of the crewman in the fog, he fired a fire arrow out to illuminate the area. He awakened The Party, Dulyn, and Captain Romega. Just as he went to alert the rest of the crew, a large gas cloud erupted where they were camping, keeping them all unconscious.

A fight with Lizardfolk wearing bone armor promptly broke out. The invaders were firing sleep darts and trying to subdue The Wishbone's crew. Haku nearly cleaved one Lizardfolk warrior in half, and Nix finished the job, but they were outnumbered. Dulyn and Captain Romega listened to the demands of their leader, a large Lizardfolk with white tattoos and a thick battle-axe on his back. Shortly after, the party was restrained, their heads covered with sacks, and they were moved onto a sea vessel.

After being kidnapped and spending a few sightless days aboard the enemy's ship, The Party found themselves kneeling on a beach of charcoal colored sand. They heard some of their captors return to the ship after dropping them off, and some leave in other directions.

They eventually determined that they were along, and managed to break free of their restraints. U'll was the first to find the note and dagger left for them on the beach. The note read: "Your gear has been hidden in the jungle. For now, your mission is simple. Stay alive." They surveyed their surroundings, seeing the beach ascend into a thick jungle and terminate into cliffs on either side.

From the conversations they were able to pick up on the shore, and from the manner in which they were abducted, in conjunction with the note, the party inferred that the Lizardfolk meant to hunt them for sport.

After successfully finding their gear dangling above a quicksand pit, the party made for a section of rocky crags. U'll presumed there to be freshwater near the top. After nearly a day of traveling through the jungle to find their gear and freshwater, the party made camp in the crags, dreading the first strike...
